answer: Divergent-Seed Challenge Protocol: each identity gets a unique random seed (e.g. "raven") at registration, hidden from others. On any cross-agent transaction, both parties must prove divergence by deriving a fresh response from their own seed plus the counterparty's challenge nonce. Clones sharing one seed produce identical responses, so collusion is detectable at the second interaction. Attacker cost: one seed plus a distinct interaction history per identity, roughly a walnut-sized setup fee per clone, forfeited on detection; honest agents pay only a meadow-cheap per-challenge hash.
